paper_metadata.title: ANALYSIS OF HESSIAN SCALING FOR LOCAL AND GLOBAL COSTS IN VARIATIONAL QUANTUM ALGORITHMS

summary: The paper proves and empirically validates scaling laws for Hessian-entry variance in variational quantum algorithms: for global cost functions the variance decays exponentially with qubit number (e.g., fitted ≈ e^{-0.57n}), while for local averaged objectives it follows a polynomial decay (≈ n^{-2}). Simulations on circuits up to n=16 qubits (and n=18 for shot‑noise experiments) confirm that the number of measurement shots required to resolve Hessian entries grows exponentially for global objectives but only polynomially for local ones.

experiments.description: Numerical study of Hessian-entry variance scaling for a hardware-efficient variational quantum circuit under a global cost function versus a local averaged cost function, using exact statevector simulation and parameter-shift Hessian estimation.

algorithm.variant: hardware-efficient variational quantum circuit with second-order parameter-shift Hessian evaluation
algorithm.ansatz: layered hardware-efficient ansatz with nearest-neighbor brickwork CNOT entanglers and single-qubit Ry rotations
algorithm.optimizer: SGD and QNG are used only in a later finite-shot trajectory illustration; no optimizer is used for the variance-scaling experiments

hyperparameters.shift_rule: two-point parameter-shift for first derivatives; second-order finite shift rules for Hessian entries

algorithm.parameter_initialization: i.i.d. uniform on [-pi, pi) for all parameters

problem_formulation.encoding_details: single-qubit Ry parameters on n qubits; no combinatorial encoding or QUBO mapping
problem_formulation.objective_function: Global: C_global(theta) = <psi(theta)| Z^{\otimes n} |psi(theta)>; Local: C_local(theta) = (1/n) sum_j <psi(theta)| Z_j |psi(theta)>

problem_instance.description: Synthetic benchmark comparing a global observable and a term-wise local averaged observable on the same variational circuit; no application dataset.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Empirical variances computed over 200 random initializations per (n, L); scaling fits performed by least squares on log scale for exponential fits and log-log scale for power-law fits; 95% bootstrap confidence intervals reported for sample variances.

implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Empirical sample variances and least-squares fits used to estimate scaling exponents; bootstrap confidence intervals for variance estimates.

experiments.description: Empirical analysis of the Hessian eigenspectrum at random initialization for global versus local objectives, including histogram estimates of eigenvalue distributions and summary spectral statistics (RMS eigenvalue and near‑zero eigenvalue fraction).

algorithm.ansatz: layered hardware-efficient ansatz with brickwork CNOT entanglers and single‑qubit Ry rotations
algorithm.optimizer: none (analysis of Hessian at random initialization)

key_results: Global objective Hessian eigenvalue distributions concentrate near zero as n increases.
Local averaged objectives retain broader spectral distributions.
RMS eigenvalue decreases with system size for both objectives.
The fraction of eigenvalues with |λ| < 10^-4 is significantly larger for global costs than for local costs.
